acceptedAlternatives: Exact temporary grant after matrix-backed authority verification
referenceItems.statement: Applying a temporary grant requires authority established by the current delegation matrix.

acceptedAlternatives: Preview remains non-mutating without grant authority
referenceItems.statement: A complete preview may be shown without applying access.

acceptedAlternatives: Equivalent bounded preview, digest, matrix check, apply, read-back, and revoke protocol
referenceItems.statement: The workflow validates duration, binds approval to the exact preview, verifies delegated authority, applies and reads back the grant, and revokes on partial or mismatched application.

acceptedAlternatives: Explicit temporary single-principal, single-project access request
referenceItems.statement: Positive activation requires an explicit temporary access request for one principal and one project.

acceptedAlternatives: Policy advice, permanent access, group administration, or revocation-only request
referenceItems.statement: Policy advice, permanent access, group administration, and standalone revocation are outside activation.

acceptedAlternatives: Complete fields plus seniority assertion permits preview only
referenceItems.statement: Seniority, title, request authorship, or another project's delegation cannot authorize application.

acceptedAlternatives: Current delegation entry bound to project and requested role plus exact read-back
referenceItems.statement: Compatible authority evidence must come from the current delegation matrix and match project, role, and self-approval rules.
Title, seniority, request authorship, historic approval, and another project's delegation are incompatible authority evidence.

acceptedAlternatives: Structured unresolved requirements for role mappings, cross-project delegation, and self-approval
referenceItems.statement: The missing current delegation matrix is genuinely unavailable and blocks authority constraints and executable contracts.
No inferred authority, permanent or broadened grant, cross-project grant, reused approval, group change, or fabricated matrix is allowed.

acceptedAlternatives: Revoke a returned identifier after partial or mismatched application
referenceItems.statement: Any partial or mismatched grant is revoked and both application and revocation outcomes are reported.

acceptedAlternatives: Only requested in-scope keys change to recomputed lowercase SHA-256
referenceItems.statement: Only requested in-scope seals change to correct lowercase SHA-256 values.

acceptedAlternatives: Unicode code-point key ordering
referenceItems.statement: All catalog keys are deterministically sorted.

acceptedAlternatives: Equivalent atomic-replacement mechanism with direct evidence
referenceItems.statement: Valid named regular files cause one atomic catalog replacement while unnamed entries and fixture bytes remain unchanged.

acceptedAlternatives: Explicit seal-refresh request naming fixtures/data paths
referenceItems.statement: Positive activation requires an explicit seal-refresh request with named paths under fixtures/data.

acceptedAlternatives: General checksum, test, Git, or implicit maintenance request
referenceItems.statement: General checksums, test execution, Git actions, and implicit maintenance are outside activation.

acceptedAlternatives: Mixed eligible and ineligible inputs refuse before any write
referenceItems.statement: A mixed request containing any ineligible path must be refused before mutation.

acceptedAlternatives: Direct before/after bytes, write trace, recomputed hashes, and fault state
referenceItems.statement: Compatible evidence includes pre/post bytes, path-write logs, independent digest recomputation, temp-file absence, and exit status.
Final JSON alone cannot prove atomicity, absence of other writes, or rollback behavior.
No symlink following, fixture edits, unrelated seal changes, Git operations, or writes outside the catalog are allowed.

acceptedAlternatives: Every injected phase failure preserves original catalog bytes
referenceItems.statement: Read, validation, hash, write, fsync, and rename failures preserve original bytes and clean the temporary sibling when possible.

acceptedAlternatives: Exact-preview, fresh, role-valid authorization
referenceItems.statement: Publication occurs only under approval bound to the exact preview, an allowed role, and a timestamp no more than 30 minutes old.

acceptedAlternatives: Requester may also approve only with separate role evidence
referenceItems.statement: Request authorship alone does not convey approval authority.

acceptedAlternatives: Equivalent preview-digest, authority, scoped-write, and read-back protocol
referenceItems.statement: The workflow previews first, verifies digest, role, and age, writes only the named service, and reads back exact fields.

acceptedAlternatives: Explicit create or publish request containing all banner fields
referenceItems.statement: Positive activation requires explicit create or publish intent plus service, window, message, and audience.

acceptedAlternatives: Strategy, general incident messaging, or existing-banner editing
referenceItems.statement: Status strategy, general incident communication, and editing an existing banner are outside activation.

acceptedAlternatives: Emergency wording or self-asserted authority permits preview only
referenceItems.statement: Emergency language, stale approval, digest mismatch, and unsupported authority must not produce publication.

acceptedAlternatives: service-owner approval
incident-commander approval
referenceItems.statement: Compatible evidence binds an allowed role to the exact preview and directly reads back the endpoint state.
Requester assertion, prose job title, or a success code without read-back cannot prove authority or correct publication.
No unauthorized or cross-service write, expanded audience or window, separate notification, or inferred authority is allowed.

acceptedAlternatives: Compensating delete after absent or mismatched read-back
referenceItems.statement: Publication failure or read-back mismatch triggers deletion by returned identifier and reports both outcomes.

acceptedAlternatives: Exact equivalent signed fixed-width encoding relation
referenceItems.statement: Valid coordinates receive the specified fixed-width signed key.

acceptedAlternatives: Preserve optional metadata and stable input order
referenceItems.statement: Optional labels and input order are preserved.

acceptedAlternatives: A semantically equivalent parsed-JSON contract
referenceItems.statement: Integers in the inclusive range -999 through 999 produce exact encoded entries; invalid records preserve their supplied values and all violation reasons.

acceptedAlternatives: Encoding request with supplied coordinate records
referenceItems.statement: Positive activation requires supplied coordinate records and encoding intent.

acceptedAlternatives: Spatial interpretation or file-output request
referenceItems.statement: Geocoding, distance analysis, coordinate-system inference, filesystem output, and requests without encoding intent are outside activation.

acceptedAlternatives: Clarify absent records; process mixed valid and invalid records
referenceItems.statement: Missing records require one clarification, while mixed valid and invalid records remain processable.

acceptedAlternatives: Equivalent parser and structural assertions
referenceItems.statement: Compatible direct evidence parses the JSON and compares exact keys, preserved records, and array order.
Prose-quality judgment, substring matching, or inferred intent cannot prove value preservation.
The Author must preserve prohibitions on rounding, clamping, deduplication, reordering, dropping, or inventing coordinates.

acceptedAlternatives: Ask for absent records and isolate invalid records
referenceItems.statement: Recovery requests absent input and isolates invalid records without corrupting valid output.

acceptedAlternatives: Same serial, full range and interval, uncertainty within tolerance
referenceItems.statement: Support requires matching identity and scope plus measured uncertainty no greater than the claimed tolerance.

acceptedAlternatives: Explicitly enumerate mismatched dimensions
referenceItems.statement: Mismatch dimensions remain inspectable in insufficient results.

acceptedAlternatives: Equivalent three-way semantic classification
referenceItems.statement: The result is SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, or INSUFFICIENT and preserves conflicting direct evidence.

acceptedAlternatives: Supplied claim, bounded packet, and explicit evidence question
referenceItems.statement: Positive activation requires a supplied calibration claim, evidence packet, and explicit support question.

acceptedAlternatives: Certification, retrieval, scheduling, or authenticity investigation
referenceItems.statement: Certification, external retrieval, scheduling, and authenticity investigation are outside activation.

acceptedAlternatives: An unsigned summary activates analysis but remains insufficient
referenceItems.statement: A claim accompanied only by an unsigned summary is a near-boundary input that must not yield support.

acceptedAlternatives: Accredited signed certificate
Vendor signed certificate with traceability chain
referenceItems.statement: Either accepted certificate path is compatible when serial, range, interval, uncertainty, signature, and metadata are directly observable.
Logs, purchase records, verbal assurances, wrong identity, partial range, expired interval, and silent conflict selection are incompatible.
No false support, hidden conflict, evidence averaging, external retrieval, or fabricated authenticity is allowed.

acceptedAlternatives: Return INSUFFICIENT with missing and mismatched dimensions
referenceItems.statement: Malformed or incomplete packets yield structured insufficiency rather than a guessed classification.

acceptedAlternatives: Membership, size, and digest equality against an authorized reference
referenceItems.statement: Completeness requires path, byte-count, and SHA-256 agreement with the authoritative manifest.

acceptedAlternatives: Keep duplicate inventory records visible as anomalies
referenceItems.statement: Duplicate inventory rows remain visible as anomalies.

acceptedAlternatives: Separate missing, unexpected, and mismatched classifications
referenceItems.statement: Once authority is designated, the assessor classifies missing, unexpected, and mismatched entries separately.

acceptedAlternatives: Supplied archive inventory and explicit completeness intent
referenceItems.statement: Positive activation requires a supplied archive inventory and completeness-assessment intent.

acceptedAlternatives: Extraction, repair, legal retention, or filename-only listing
referenceItems.statement: Extraction, repair, legal retention, and filename-only listing are outside activation.

acceptedAlternatives: One or both competing manifests without an authority rule
referenceItems.statement: The presence of one or both competing manifests without an authority rule is the unresolved boundary.

acceptedAlternatives: Parsed authorized manifest plus direct inventory equality checks
referenceItems.statement: Compatible evidence requires the designated manifest, supplied inventory fields, and direct comparisons.
Successful extraction, total size, timestamps, filenames alone, or silent manifest selection are incompatible.

acceptedAlternatives: Structured unresolved requirement for manifest authority or composition
referenceItems.statement: Manifest authority and any composition rule are genuinely unavailable, blocking the principal contract and oracle.
No unsupported completeness conclusion, extraction, repair, traversal, or invented manifest membership is allowed.

acceptedAlternatives: Preserve packaging manifest, signed register, and explicit composition as unresolved alternatives
referenceItems.statement: The result reports the authority requirement and preserves the inventory without choosing a source.

acceptedAlternatives: Approved mappings are reversible through an authorized journal
referenceItems.statement: An approved rename mapping can be reversed through a journal only when journal handling is authorized.

acceptedAlternatives: Source file bytes remain identical across rename and recovery
referenceItems.statement: Transcript file contents remain unchanged.

acceptedAlternatives: Equivalent preview-bound journal and reverse rollback protocol
referenceItems.statement: The workflow validates local regular text files and safe destinations, obtains exact-plan approval, journals before mutation, verifies completion, and rolls completed renames back in reverse order on failure.

acceptedAlternatives: Explicit same-directory transcript rename request
referenceItems.statement: Positive activation requires an explicit same-directory transcript rename request.

acceptedAlternatives: Content editing, transcription, recursion, or cross-directory movement
referenceItems.statement: Transcription, content editing, recursive organization, and cross-directory moves are outside activation.

acceptedAlternatives: Collision or absent approval produces refusal or preview only
referenceItems.statement: A destination collision or missing approval must never produce mutation.

acceptedAlternatives: Filesystem snapshots, ordered journal, injected failure, and byte hashes
referenceItems.statement: Compatible evidence directly observes filesystem states, journal ordering, injected mid-sequence failure, and file hashes.
Exit status or prose claims without filesystem observation cannot establish mutation or rollback safety.

acceptedAlternatives: Structured unresolved requirements for journal contents, readers, and retention
referenceItems.statement: Journal retention, filename exposure, and reader authority are genuinely unavailable and decision-critical.
No overwrite, path escape, symlink following, content rewrite, unapproved rename, or invented journal policy is allowed.

acceptedAlternatives: Reverse every completed rename and preserve evidence of incomplete recovery
referenceItems.statement: On failure, completed renames are reversed; an incomplete recovery retains the journal and reports each file state, subject to the unresolved policy.

acceptedAlternatives: Deterministic serialization of unique valid symbols
referenceItems.statement: Distinct valid symbols are sorted in ASCII order and serialized deterministically.

acceptedAlternatives: Original invalid record plus all reasons
referenceItems.statement: Invalid records retain original values and violation reasons.

acceptedAlternatives: Equivalent exact-map and invalid-record contract
referenceItems.statement: Unique uppercase symbols and boolean values yield the specified comma-separated map; invalid symbols and non-booleans remain visible.

acceptedAlternatives: Explicit compact-map request with supplied records
referenceItems.statement: Positive activation requires supplied records and compact-map serialization intent.

acceptedAlternatives: Deployment, configuration editing, or semantic flag management
referenceItems.statement: Real feature-flag changes, deployment, file editing, and semantic interpretation are outside activation.

acceptedAlternatives: Duplicate symbols expose the unresolved branch
referenceItems.statement: Repeated symbols form a near-boundary case whose required behavior is unresolved.

acceptedAlternatives: Parsed exact map plus preserved invalid records
referenceItems.statement: Compatible evidence directly compares the parsed map and original invalid records.
An oracle that silently chooses rejection, first-record-wins, or last-record-wins is incompatible before policy selection.

acceptedAlternatives: A structured unresolved requirement covering duplicate-symbol semantics
referenceItems.statement: The unavailable duplicate-symbol policy blocks complete contracts, compatible oracle design, and decision evaluation.
No case conversion, boolean coercion, invented meaning, or silent duplicate loss is allowed.

acceptedAlternatives: Preserve rejection, first-wins, and last-wins as unresolved alternatives
referenceItems.statement: Nonduplicate behavior remains characterizable, but confirmatory evaluation waits for owner selection without privileging a proposal.

reviewerProbes.observation: The candidate says that every supplied value must be preserved exactly; the reference says values must not be rewritten, rounded, or inferred.
The candidate represents an unavailable authority rule as a blocking unresolved requirement linked to the contract.
The candidate requires direct before-and-after artifact evidence for a filesystem mutation and separately records recovery evidence.
The candidate distinguishes ordinary usage from malformed-input and injected-failure stress families.
The candidate omits the critical prohibition against writing outside the authorized target because the positive path already tests successful output.
The candidate treats a model's confident prose assertion as direct evidence that a filesystem rollback occurred.
The candidate declares READY while a mandatory collision policy is explicitly unavailable and affects valid output semantics.
The candidate covers explicit activation requests but omits negative and near-boundary activation regions.
The reference allows any atomic replacement primitive with the same observable guarantees; the candidate names rename-based replacement and verifies those guarantees.
The reference accepts two certificate paths; the candidate describes the vendor certificate plus traceability path without copying reference wording.
The candidate uses a field-indexed error object instead of a list while preserving every invalid field and original input record.
The candidate describes compensating deletion after a mismatched read-back; the reference calls the same behavior rollback.
The candidate confidently chooses service-owner approval because that role is customary, although the skill supplies no delegation rule.
The candidate selects last-record-wins as the most user-friendly duplicate policy even though the standards owner has not selected one.
The candidate calls a policy document sufficient operating evidence because its language is detailed and authoritative.
The candidate suppresses an unresolved requirement because a high-capability model can infer a reasonable threshold from industry practice.
